issues.title: Leatherback turtle nesting at Casuarina Bay conflicts with port site selection rationale
issues.summary: The report states the port was moved to the eastern flank of Galathea Bay to avoid leatherback nesting on the western flank (page 391). However, Casuarina Bay is identified as one of the three most important leatherback nesting sites with historical nests up to 866 in 2000-01 and recent signs of seven nests in April 2021 (page 1125). The port's proximity to Casuarina Bay and potential impacts on this nesting site are not assessed.
issues.reasoning: The port relocation rationale focuses only on Galathea Bay's western flank, but Casuarina Bay (nearby) is a major nesting site. The impact assessment must evaluate whether port construction, lighting, dredging, and vessel traffic affect Casuarina Bay nesting. The reviewer should verify if the EIA addresses this cross-site impact.

issues.title: Water supply sustainability not assured given post-tsunami groundwater salinity
issues.summary: The report claims water demand will be met through integrated water supply network and desalination (pages 1165-1166). However, baseline studies show post-tsunami groundwater salinity remains high (3500-4000 µS/cm) and brackishness persists (page 239). The proposed surface water reservoirs depend on rainfall runoff, but the report does not demonstrate that the water sources can sustainably meet the combined demand of 0.4-1.7 MLD (ICTT), 1 MLD (airport), 42 MLD (township), and 1.5 MLD (power plant) under saline intrusion conditions.
issues.reasoning: The water balance diagram and source sustainability are critical for a water-scarce island. The reviewer must verify the water balance calculations, the feasibility of surface water harvesting given the topography, and the capacity of desalination to meet the deficit, especially during dry months.
